answer: A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, since the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. The echo multiplier is published, charged in delta, and island lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 18 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 3089 identities would post 910 proofs and burn roughly 49 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
